profile.reading: Per CyrusOne own facility page for Quincy, Washington (PNW1), this facility publishes 36 MW of total IT capacity and 720,000 square feet of technical IT space, at a street address of 1025 D Street Northwest, Quincy, WA 98848. CyrusOne describes the site as located about halfway between Seattle and Spokane, and as the largest greenfield built facility the company has developed in Washington state, with additional land reserved for future development subject to power availability.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Quincy campus publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 720,000 square feet of technical space, the largest single disclosed data center footprint in Washington state.

This facility represents roughly 900 racks at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack. The operator describes it as the largest greenfield facility CyrusOne has built in Washington state and notes that additional land is reserved for expansion, but explicitly constrains that expansion by power availability. This framing inverts the usual causation: the building exists and can grow, but the power grid cannot yet support it. Washington has 46 mapped data center facilities total, but only two publish power figures, so this 36 MW site accounts for 60 percent of all disclosed state capacity simply because disclosure is sparse.

The operator published no certifications or technical specifications for this facility. Whether the campus qualifies for GPU workloads, how much of the 36 MW currently serves high-density AI training versus other workloads, the amount of power needed for reserved expansion, or the timeline for that expansion remain unpublished. CyrusOne's own site does not quantify the power constraint it cites as the binding limit on growth.
